t: You're standing at numbers 1 to 15 Connaught Square, a terrace of buildings in Westminster. They were designed by George Gutch, a British architect and surveyor born in 1790. Gutch worked for four successive Bishops of London, acting as surveyor for much of the Diocese's southern strip of the parish of Paddington, an area of about five hundred acres. This square sits within that land, so it belongs to a part of London that was managed and laid out through the Church.
